subject.title: Bug: Poe image/video-output models are accepted in config but fail at runtime (Nano Banana 400, Veo/Sora fallback)

question: Should OpenClaw reject non-text-output models when configured as chat/session models, or add first-class output-modality metadata and runtime/channel support for image/video outputs?
rationale: Both paths are plausible, but the choice changes public model config semantics, fallback behavior, provider ownership, and channel rendering expectations.

options.title: Reject unsupported chat output now
options.body: Add a clear diagnostic for image/video-output models selected as chat/session models and direct users to `image_generate` or `video_generate` until first-class support exists.

options.title: Add output-modality support
options.body: Extend config/catalog metadata and runtime/channel handling so selected models can intentionally produce image/video outputs in session flow.

options.title: Docs-only clarification
options.body: Document the current tool-driven media path while leaving custom-provider chat selection behavior unchanged.

recommendation.title: Reject unsupported chat output now
recommendation.body: Add a clear diagnostic for image/video-output models selected as chat/session models and direct users to `image_generate` or `video_generate` until first-class support exists.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision crosses the image-generation tool origin, provider/model config semantics, and the core-vs-plugin product boundary reflected in recent history.
